name: Retrieval Augmented Generation Evaluation in the Era of Large Language Models: A Comprehensive Survey (Gan et al.)
venue: arXiv preprint arXiv:2504.14891 (v1 submitted 21 Apr 2025). Subjects: Computation and Language (cs.CL). 18 pages, 5 figures. arXiv-issued DOI 10.48550/arXiv.2504.14891. Semantic Scholar tags it JournalArticle/Review (journal name 'ArXiv'); no peer-reviewed conference/journal venue confirmed for this comprehensive-survey version. It directly extends the authors' earlier peer-reviewed work 'Evaluation of Retrieval-Augmented Generation: A Survey' (Yu et al.), accepted at CCF Big Data 2024 (Springer).
authors_affiliation: Aoran Gan, Hao Yu, Kai Zhang, Qi Liu, Wenyu Yan, Zhenya Huang, Shiwei Tong, Guoping Hu (8 authors on the arXiv abstract page; the HTML body also lists Enhong Chen). Primary affiliation: State Key Laboratory of Cognitive Intelligence, University of Science and Technology of China (USTC), Hefei, China. Additional affiliations: McGill University, Montreal, Canada (Hao Yu); Tencent Company, Shenzhen, China; Artificial Intelligence Research Institute, iFLYTEK Co., Ltd, Hefei, China.
code_url: N/A (a survey, not a method; no method code). It is associated with the maintained 'Awesome-RAG-Evaluation' paper-list/benchmark-list repo (see maintained_repo_url).
maintained_repo_url: https://github.com/YHPeter/Awesome-RAG-Evaluation (the official GitHub repository whose citation block explicitly cites this paper, arXiv:2504.14891; it catalogs RAG evaluation frameworks/benchmarks with code and paper links and was updated 2025-04-21 to 'Add new benchmarks for RAG system'. The repo was originally created for the predecessor CCF Big Data 2024 survey 'Evaluation of RAG: A Survey'/Auepora, which this work extends; ~198 stars).
task_domain: Survey of RAG evaluation. The surveyed systems target knowledge-intensive QA as the prevailing operationalization (RAG assessments are typically converted into a QA/conversational format of question + ground-truth answer + candidate docs), plus downstream domains catalogued via benchmarks: medical, legal, finance, telecom, multilingual, multi-turn, long-context. Not about planning/agents/tool-use/embodied; it explicitly scopes to the narrow training-free RAG framework over unstructured documents and excludes knowledge-graph and multimodal RAG evaluation.
problem_setting: A comprehensive literature survey (not a method) of how to evaluate RAG systems in the LLM era. It deconstructs a RAG system into retriever and generator components and organizes evaluation into Internal Evaluation (component-level: retrieval and generation, conventional IR/NLG metrics, and LLM-based metrics) versus External Evaluation (system-level utility: Safety and Efficiency), framed via a systems-theory internal/external lens that extends the authors' earlier Auepora unified evaluation process. The surveyed setting is predominantly offline, single-agent, non-interactive, training-free RAG over unstructured external documents; supervision ranges from off-the-shelf metrics to LLM-as-judge. It also performs a meta-analysis (research-oriented meta-evaluation) over 582 peer-reviewed RAG papers crawled from high-level NLP/AI venues since autumn 2022 to quantify which evaluation methods are actually used.
what_is_retrieved: docs (unstructured text documents / chunks). The survey scopes to unstructured text retrieval as the prevailing paradigm and explicitly excludes knowledge-graph and multimodal retrieval; only datasets that contain retrieved ground-truth documents are included in its dataset table. It does not survey retrieval of demos/cases/trajectories/skills/tools/experiences/guidelines (that agentic-experience family is out of scope).
retrieval_grounding: STATIC external corpus is the dominant grounding surveyed (a corpus is constructed offline via chunking + embedding; sources include Wikipedia, specialized corpora such as scientific articles and financial reports). The survey also notes real-time / dynamic knowledge sources (web scraping, search engines, live news) and time-sensitive benchmarks (FreshLLMs/FreshQA, MultiHop-RAG, CDQA, CRAG) that depend on rapidly updated documents - i.e. dynamic-but-external grounding, not an agent-written growing memory. So: predominantly static external corpus, with a notable dynamic/real-time-corpus dimension; not episodic agent memory.
completeness_vs_topk_objective: The default retrieval objective surveyed is a fixed top-k document ranking (Recall@K / Precision@K / NDCG@K / Hit@K over top-k retrieved docs). The survey additionally elevates 'Comprehensiveness' (Relevant Documents <-> Relevant Documents) as an explicit retrieval evaluation target measuring diversity and coverage so that retrieved docs give a comprehensive view of the topic - a coverage/completeness-flavored objective distinct from precision-only top-k. It does not frame the goal as a precision-driven variable-size recommendation.
retrieval_unit: Document / text chunk. The survey describes offline chunking that segments large documents into smaller manageable units, then embedding for retrieval; the retrieved unit evaluated is the relevant document/passage/chunk (it scopes to unstructured documents and excludes KG-subgraph and multimodal units).
index_source: Static, offline-constructed retrievable store is the dominant case (corpus built before retrieval via offline chunking + embedding into a vector index). The survey also covers dynamic/online sources (search-engine queries, real-time web/news scraping) used by time-sensitive benchmarks. As a survey it is not itself inducing an index; it catalogs static-corpus and dynamic-external-corpus construction. Not an online/test-time agent-induced memory.
index_structure_topology: Flat vector index over embedded chunks is the surveyed default (text vectorized into a high-dimensional dense semantic space for efficient retrieval). The survey notes online-RAG add-ons (intent recognition, query rewriting, routing) and multiple retrieval strategies (sparse/dense/graph/hybrid), but it explicitly scopes the main paradigm to unstructured-document flat-index retrieval and excludes graph/structured indices from its evaluation focus.
retriever_type: Surveyed across types: sparse retrieval (BM25-style), dense retrieval (embedding-based, the default), graph retrieval, and hybrid methods. Some commercialized systems perform additional dynamic search-engine queries. The survey does not endorse one retriever; for its evaluation scope dense/sparse/hybrid over unstructured text is the prevailing setting.
retriever_learning_signal: N/A as a contribution - this is an evaluation survey, not a retriever-training method, so it does not train a retriever. It scopes to the training-free RAG framework. Where relevant it notes retrievers are typically off-the-shelf dense/sparse embedding models within the surveyed systems; the survey's focus is on how to score retrieval quality (Relevance/Comprehensiveness/Correctness via IR metrics and LLM-based judges), not on retriever optimization signals.
query_construction: Surveyed as part of the online RAG workflow: raw query plus optional pre-retrieval components - intent recognition, query rewriting, and routing - introduced before retrieval. RAG assessments commonly convert the task into a QA/conversational format (question + ground-truth answer + candidate docs). The survey catalogs query construction as a pipeline stage rather than proposing one.
query_granularity: Task-level / query-level is the prevailing granularity surveyed (one user query mapped to retrieved docs then a response), with the QA-format conversion of question -> answer. Multi-turn and bridging-query benchmarks (MTRAG) and multi-hop cross-document benchmarks (MultiHop-RAG) are catalogued, which involve trajectory/turn-level querying, but the dominant evaluated unit is the single query.
when_to_retrieve: One-shot retrieve-then-generate is the prevailing surveyed paradigm (retrieve documents, then the LLM synthesizes a response). The survey notes online workflows with pre-retrieval routing and post-retrieval reranking/fusion and discusses multi-hop/multi-turn benchmarks, but iterative/active/adaptive retrieval is not the organizing axis of this evaluation survey (it inherits the standard retriever->generator pipeline).
retrieval_trigger_signal: N/A / fixed schedule. As an evaluation survey over the standard retriever->generator pipeline, retrieval is triggered once per query by the pipeline; the survey does not center an adaptive WHEN-to-retrieve signal (token confidence, learned classifier, reflection tokens). Robustness/safety evaluation does probe whether the system should keep vs discard retrieved context (Chen et al.'s answerable/unanswerable x keep/discard Risk/Carefulness/Alignment/Coverage metrics), which is closest to a retrieval-use decision.
reranking: Yes - reranking is surveyed as an optional post-retrieval step where some systems rerank documents or fuse data across sources before generation. A 'Diversity Reranker' framework (using Cosine Distances) is catalogued in the frameworks table (Table 2). Reranking is treated as a pipeline component whose effect is evaluated, not as the survey's own contribution.
retrieved_context_refinement: Surveyed as pipeline stages: post-retrieval reranking and cross-source data fusion before generation, and (on the generation side) prompt-engineering scaffolds applied to retrieved context such as CoT, Tree-of-Thoughts (ToT), Self-Note, and RaR (Rephrase-and-Respond). Post-processing after generation (e.g. entity recognition for multiple-choice/classification, translation for multilingual tasks) is also noted. The survey catalogs these refinements rather than proposing a single one.
how_retrieved_used: Prompt augmentation: retrieved relevant documents are passed to the LLM, which acts as a decision-maker/reasoner that synthesizes the retrieved information into a coherent response (rather than generating knowledge independently), thereby reducing hallucination. The survey's focus is on evaluating whether that synthesis is Relevant, Faithful (grounded in the docs), and Correct (matches the gold answer).
planning_integration: N/A / out of scope. This is a RAG-evaluation survey over the retriever->generator pipeline; it does not cover planning, MCTS/tree-search, or hierarchical subtask planning. The closest analog is the standard retrieve-then-generate flow plus prompt-engineering reasoning scaffolds (CoT/ToT) inside the generator.
reasoning_search_interleaving_granularit: Per-answer (single retrieve-then-generate per query is the prevailing evaluated unit). The survey notes generation-side reasoning scaffolds (CoT/ToT/Self-Note) and multi-hop/multi-turn benchmarks, and flags evaluating deep-thinking models (e.g. OpenAI o1) interleaved with RAG retrieval/generation as an under-explored future direction - implying finer-grained interleaving is not yet standard in surveyed evaluations.
retrieved_item_representation: Raw retrieved text documents/passages injected as prompt context for the generator. The survey evaluates the surface response against the retrieved documents (Faithfulness) and against the gold answer (Correctness); it does not survey distilled-strategy/workflow/program/latent representations (out of scope for unstructured-document RAG).
abstraction_level_of_retrieved_unit: Raw retrieved documents/passages (single retrieved document/chunk granularity). No distilled strategy, workflow, skill, or hint abstraction - the survey scopes to unstructured-text knowledge retrieval, not experience/skill retrieval.
noise_robustness_mechanism: Central evaluation theme rather than a method. The survey catalogs how RAG robustness to irrelevant/misleading/counterfactual retrieved context is measured and benchmarked: RGB (noise robustness, negative rejection, information integration, counterfactual robustness with Accuracy); RECALL (reliable vs counterfactual knowledge via BLEU/ROUGE-L and Misleading Rate); Wu et al. Misrepresentation Ratio / Uncertainty Ratio for semantically-related-but-irrelevant info; SafeRAG (inter-context conflict); C-RAG (conformal risk analysis / theoretical risk guarantees); Cheng et al. Resilience Rate and Boost Rate; and Chen et al.'s Risk/Carefulness/Alignment/Coverage for keep-vs-discard decisions. These are evaluation/diagnostic mechanisms, not a training-time defense the survey itself proposes.
memory_type: none (classic RAG over static/dynamic external documents; the survey scopes to training-free unstructured-document RAG and does not center episodic/skill/workflow/graph/latent agent memory).
write_back: false. The surveyed RAG paradigm reads from an external corpus and does not write new experiences/cases back into a memory store. The survey is about evaluating retrieval+generation quality, not memory accumulation.
online_growth: Mostly false (the corpus/index is constructed offline and read at inference). The survey does note dynamic external knowledge sources (real-time news/web scraping, search engines) and time-varying benchmarks (FreshQA, CDQA, CRAG) whose underlying corpora update over time - external corpus dynamism rather than an agent-written growing memory.
write_back_trigger: never (no experience/case write-back in the surveyed training-free document-RAG paradigm; retrieval is read-only over an external corpus).
failure_experience_usage: Not a focus / N/A. The survey does not store the system's own success/failure trajectories. The closest related ideas it catalogs are robustness/safety evaluations of how the system handles incorrect or adversarial retrieved documents (RECALL counterfactuals, PoisonedRAG corpus poisoning, hallucination-rate measurement), i.e. evaluating responses to bad context, not storing failed experiences.
memory_evolution_update: N/A (no stored experiential entries to mutate in the surveyed document-RAG paradigm). External-corpus updates (live news, dynamic QA benchmarks) are offline data refreshes rather than online entry-level memory evolution.
retrieval_as_learned_policy: No / N/A. Retrieval is treated as standard similarity-based top-k over a document index in the surveyed training-free framework; the survey does not present retrieval/case-selection as a learned or RL-optimized policy (its contribution is evaluation methodology, not retrieval optimization).
cross_agent_or_cross_framework_sharing: N/A / not a focus. The survey covers single-system RAG pipelines and does not center cross-agent or cross-framework shared memory. It does compile cross-framework evaluation resources (Table 2) so practitioners can compare evaluation frameworks, but that is a catalog of evaluation tools, not shared agent memory.
benchmarks: Catalogs RAG-specific benchmarks/datasets (Table 1) and evaluation frameworks (Table 2). Benchmarks/datasets include: WikiEval (RAGAS), FreshQA (FreshLLMs), RECALL (EventKG/UJ), ARES (reusing NQ, HotpotQA, FEVER, WoW, MultiRC, ReCoRD from KILT and SuperGLUE), RGB, MultiHop-RAG, CRUD-RAG (with UHGEval), MedRAG (MIRAGE), FeB4RAG (with BEIR), RAGBench (PubMedQA, CovidQA, HotpotQA, MS MARCO, CUAD, DelucionQA, EManual, TechQA, FinQA, TAT-QA; TRACe), ReEval (NQ-MRQA + RealTimeQA), DomainRAG, Telecom RAG Eval (TeleQuAD, 3GPP), LegalBench-RAG (PrivacyQA, CUAD, MAUD, ContractNLI), RAGEval (DragonBall: finance/law/medical), CoURAGE (RealTimeQA + NQ), RAG Unfairness (TREC22 FairRank, BBQ), CoFE-RAG, OCR-Hinders-RAG (1,261 PDFs + 8,561 images / OHR-Bench), OmniEval (finance), CRAG (KG + web), RAG Playground (319 QA pairs), MTRAG (CLAPNQ, FiQA, Govt, Cloud), CDQA (Chinese Dynamic QA), U-NIAH (Starlight Academy long-context needle-in-haystack), SCARF, Arabic RAG Eval. Frameworks/tools (Table 2): RAGAS, ARES, RGB, TruEra/TruLens RAG Triad, LangChain Benchmarks, Databricks Eval, FiD-Light, Diversity Reranker, RECALL, FreshLLMs/FRESHEVAL, RAGBench/TRACe, eRAG, RAGChecker-style, SafeRAG, RAGTruth-style, etc. Underlying classic QA/IR datasets referenced: NQ, HotpotQA, FEVER, MS MARCO, BEIR, KILT, SuperGLUE.
benchmark_family: QA-centric: general/single-hop QA (NQ, MS MARCO, RealTimeQA), multi-hop QA (HotpotQA, MultiHop-RAG, 2Wiki-style), long-form/needle long-context (U-NIAH), fact-checking (FEVER), domain QA (medical MedRAG/MIRAGE/PubMedQA/CovidQA, legal LegalBench-RAG/CUAD/MAUD/ContractNLI, finance OmniEval/FinQA/TAT-QA/FiQA, telecom TeleQuAD/3GPP), multilingual (Arabic RAG Eval, Chinese CRUD-RAG/CDQA), multi-turn (MTRAG), dynamic/time-sensitive (FreshQA, CDQA, CRAG), robustness/counterfactual (RGB, RECALL, ReEval), safety (SafeRAG, PoisonedRAG, RECALL), fairness (RAG Unfairness/BBQ/TREC FairRank), OCR-noise (OHR-Bench). Standard IR collections: BEIR, KILT, SuperGLUE. This is the RAG-evaluation benchmark family - NOT the agent/web/embodied/tool families (Mind2Web/WebArena/ALFWorld/ToolBench).
baselines: N/A (a survey, not a method; it runs no head-to-head method comparison). Its comparative work is (1) comparing evaluation targets/metrics for retrieval (Relevance/Comprehensiveness/Correctness) vs generation (Relevance/Faithfulness/Correctness); (2) comparing conventional IR/NLG metrics vs LLM-based (output-based and representation-based) metrics; (3) comparing evaluation frameworks side-by-side in Table 2; and (4) a meta-analysis comparing the actual usage frequency of traditional vs LLM-based metrics across 582 peer-reviewed RAG papers. It positions itself against prior RAG surveys, especially the authors' own predecessor Auepora (Yu et al.).
key_metrics: Surveys (does not report its own) the metric landscape. IR metrics: non-rank-based Accuracy/Hit@K, Recall@K, Precision@K, F1; rank-based MRR, NDCG@k (DCG/IDCG), MAP. NLG metrics: EM, ROUGE (ROUGE-N/L/W/S), BLEU, METEOR (plus BertScore). LLM-based output metrics: RAGAS/Databricks LLM-as-judge prompts, GPT-4 few-shot match, AST-based hallucination (Gorilla/Patil), SePer (Semantic Perplexity), KPR (Key Point Recall), MRWR/MRLR, FactScore and D-FActScore, and risk-aware Risk/Carefulness/Alignment/Coverage. LLM-representation metrics: GPTScore, ARES (classifier + LLM embeddings), RAGAS answer-relevance cosine, Thrust. Safety metrics: Misleading Rate, Misrepresentation/Uncertainty Ratio, Attack Success Rate (ASR), Retrieval Failure Rate, Citation Precision/Recall, Hallucination Rate, Extraction Success Rate, PII Leakage Rate, Membership-Inference success, Resilience Rate, Boost Rate. Efficiency metrics: Time-to-First-Token (TTFT), total/end-to-end latency, Single Query Latency, token-based cost, Cost-Effectiveness Ratio.
headline_result: N/A (no single experimental headline number - it is a survey). Its headline contributions are (1) the internal-vs-external evaluation taxonomy for RAG and the dual evaluation-target framework (retrieval: Relevance/Comprehensiveness/Correctness; generation: Relevance/Faithfulness/Correctness); and (2) a meta-analysis over 582 peer-reviewed RAG papers (crawled from high-level NLP/AI venues since autumn 2022) finding that traditional metrics still predominate over LLM-based evaluation methods, while LLM-based evaluation usage is rising (peaking in 2024 H2 and 2025 H1) and that internal (retrieval/generation) evaluation vastly outweighs external (safety/efficiency), with safety the most neglected.
ablations: N/A (no experiments, hence no ablations). The analytical equivalents are the meta-analysis breakdowns: (1) distribution of evaluation methods across the four segments Retrieval / Generation / Safety / Efficiency (Figure 3), showing internal >> external and safety least covered; (2) word-frequency word-cloud of metrics (Figure 4) showing traditional metrics dominate over LLM-based (-LLM-suffixed) metrics; (3) per-half-year count of papers explicitly using LLM-based RAG evaluation (Figure 5), rising with 2024 H2 and 2025 H1 highest.
evaluation_decoupling: Yes - decoupling is a core organizing principle. The survey explicitly separates retrieval-component evaluation (intrinsic IR metrics: Recall@K/Precision@K/NDCG/MRR/MAP, and targets Relevance/Comprehensiveness/Correctness) from generation-component evaluation (Faithfulness/Correctness/Relevance, NLG and LLM-based metrics), and further separates internal (component) from external (system safety/efficiency) evaluation. This component-decoupled view is the central distinction from end-to-end-only RAG evaluation.
process_vs_outcome_metrics: Both, and the survey argues for going beyond outcome-only scoring. Outcome: final-answer EM/F1/Accuracy/ROUGE/BLEU. Process/intermediate: retrieval-quality IR metrics (Recall@K/NDCG/MRR) score the retrieval step; Faithfulness scores whether generation is grounded in retrieved docs; KPR scores incorporation of key points from retrieved docs; SePer/Thrust probe internal belief/knowledgeability. The survey critiques that many components are still evaluated only via end-to-end RAG-ontology metrics and calls for more functional-decomposition and reasoning-process (e.g. deep-thinking-model) evaluation.
cost_efficiency_tradeoff: A first-class external-evaluation dimension (Section 4.2). Latency: Time-to-First-Token (TTFT) and complete/end-to-end response time (retrieval + processing + generation), plus Hofstatter et al.'s Single Query Latency. Cost: categorized into infrastructure, token-based API expenses, storage, operational overhead, and development costs; LLM-provider token-usage metrics multiplied by pricing rates; and a Cost-Effectiveness Ratio (performance improvement per unit cost). The survey flags the high cost of thorough RAG evaluation itself (vast scale of tools/datasets) and balancing cost vs effectiveness as an open challenge. No single numeric headline is given.
context_budget_and_selection_count: Discussed via chunking strategy (segmenting documents into manageable units guided by original structure/context) and top-k retrieval (Recall@K/Precision@K with a chosen k), with optional reranking/fusion to curate which retrieved docs reach the generator's prompt. Long-context handling is benchmarked separately (U-NIAH needle-in-haystack for extremely long contexts). The survey does not prescribe a single token budget; k and chunk size are treated as configurable pipeline choices whose effects are evaluated.
survey_scope_and_axes: Explicit organizing axes: (1) Internal vs External evaluation (systems-theory framing); (2) within Internal: Evaluation Target (retrieval: Relevance/Comprehensiveness/Correctness; generation: Relevance/Faithfulness/Correctness), Conventional methods (IR metrics: non-rank-based + rank-based; NLG metrics) vs LLM-based methods (Output-based vs Representation-based); (3) within External: Safety (robustness, factuality, adversarial attacks, privacy, fairness, transparency/accountability) and Efficiency (latency, cost); (4) Resources: a dataset/benchmark catalog (Table 1) and an evaluation-framework catalog (Table 2, categorized as Research/Tool/Benchmark with retrieval/generation/safety/efficiency targets). Scope is explicitly limited to training-free RAG over unstructured documents, excluding KG and multimodal RAG. Coverage: 124 references; meta-analysis over 582 peer-reviewed RAG papers since autumn 2022 through 31 March 2025.
benchmark_construction_and_size: N/A as a new benchmark (this is a survey, not a benchmark paper - it constructs no new dataset). It catalogs existing RAG-evaluation benchmarks with their construction methods in Table 1 (e.g. real-time-news sourcing for FreshQA/MultiHop-RAG/CDQA; domain-corpus curation for MedRAG/LegalBench-RAG/OmniEval; LLM-synthesized/schema-based generation with false-premise/counterfactual elements for RAGEval/RECALL; OCR-noise from 1,261 PDFs + 8,561 images). Its own empirical artifact is the meta-analysis corpus of 582 peer-reviewed RAG manuscripts crawled from high-level NLP/AI venues.
builds_on: Directly extends the authors' own predecessor survey 'Evaluation of Retrieval-Augmented Generation: A Survey' (Yu et al., the Auepora unified evaluation process; CCF Big Data 2024 / arXiv 2405.07437, reference [21]), broadening it with internal/external systems framing, LLM-based evaluation methods, safety/efficiency, and a 582-paper meta-analysis. Builds on foundational RAG formulations (retriever+generator) and the broader RAG survey lineage (e.g. Gao et al.), classic IR/NLG metrics (BLEU/ROUGE/METEOR; Recall/Precision/NDCG/MRR/MAP), and established RAG evaluation frameworks/benchmarks (RAGAS, ARES, RGB, RECALL, TruLens RAG Triad, FactScore).
contrasts_with: Positions itself against prior RAG surveys that mainly collect methods/applications but lack systematic evaluation discussion (e.g. Gao et al. and multimodal-RAG surveys), and especially against its own earlier Auepora review (Yu et al. [21]), which it says was largely confined to mainstream frameworks; this work claims to be the most comprehensive RAG-evaluation survey, bridging traditional and LLM-driven methods. Methodologically it contrasts conventional metrics (favored for simplicity/reliability) vs LLM-based metrics (more flexible but harder to standardize across LLM versions/prompts), and internal component evaluation vs external system (safety/efficiency) evaluation.
lineage: Surveys lineage. A RAG-evaluation-focused survey within the Surveys group, sitting downstream of foundational RAG surveys (e.g. Gao et al. 'RAG for LLMs: A Survey') and directly extending the authors' Auepora evaluation survey. It is orthogonal/complementary to the agentic-RAG, graph-RAG, and memory surveys in this collection: rather than cataloging RAG methods, it catalogs how RAG is measured (faithfulness, factual accuracy/correctness, relevance, comprehensiveness, safety, efficiency) and meta-analyzes evaluation practice, providing the evaluation vocabulary that method papers in this collection are scored against.
cbr_cycle_coverage: N/A (not a case-based-reasoning work; no Retrieve/Reuse/Revise/Retain case cycle - it is a RAG-evaluation survey over unstructured documents).
explicit_cbr_grounding: false. The survey does not frame RAG as case-based reasoning and does not cite Aamodt & Plaza / Kolodner; it treats RAG as retriever+generator over external knowledge and focuses on its evaluation.
tool_document_engineering: N/A (not about tool/skill retrieval; focuses on document/knowledge retrieval evaluation. It touches API-call accuracy only via the AST-based hallucination metric (Patil et al./Gorilla) used to evaluate correctness of external API calls, but does not analyze tool-description engineering for indexing).
index_content_separation: N/A (the survey does not center a lightweight-index-then-content / progressive-disclosure pattern). It discusses offline chunking + embedding into a vector index and top-k retrieval, but not an SOP-index-then-content separation.
dynamic_index_and_protocol: N/A (no tool API / RapidAPI / MCP / function-calling tool registry; the surveyed indices are document/vector stores. It notes some systems issue dynamic search-engine queries and that the corpus can draw on real-time web data, but this is not a synchronized tool index with CRUD auto-sync).
tool_dependency_awareness: N/A (no inter-tool dependency modeling; the survey covers document retrieval evaluation, not multi-tool dependency graphs).
adaptation_mechanism: N/A (no CBR-style case adaptation/revision; retrieved documents are injected verbatim as prompt context, and the survey's concern is evaluating the resulting generation, not adapting a retrieved case).
